name: Embroidery / textile art
material: thread stitched or woven onto/through textile support; silk and metallic threads can create fine linear and reflective effects
fabrication_process: build outlines and fills with stitch families
edge_behavior: Edges are constructed from thread direction and stitch boundaries; fuzzy thread bloom may soften close edges but not dissolve like watercolor.
color_behavior: Color is thread-based and can be highly saturated; silk changes brightness with angle; metallic threads produce directional highlights.
surface_behavior: Textile drape/weave and raised stitch relief remain visible; embroidered image is not printed ink.
composition_behavior: Design follows textile field and seam/border logic; stitch direction can model volume while retaining decorative flatness.
structural_limitations: stitches cannot become infinitely fine photographic pixels
thread must lie on or pass through textile
aging_weathering: fraying, fading, thread loss, tarnish and creases follow handling and material
museum-conserved textile may be flattened/mounted and stabilized

prompt_fragments.core: Reconstruct the image with visible thread decisions: stitch direction models form, silk sheen changes with angle, metallic accents are couched/stitched, and the ground weave remains legible between dense areas.

evaluation_criteria: thread paths are visible and purposeful

sources.supports: silk strength/thinness, fluid outlines, rich colors, calligraphy/seals in textile images
counted embroidery stitch and even tension on silk gauze

scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
